classification_vocabulary.surface: Source language parsing, elaboration, and desugaring before the formal core entry point.
classification_vocabulary.reference: Correction-critical semantic construction that belongs to the essential proof boundary.
classification_vocabulary.reference_extension: Correction-relevant obligation or invariant extension that must be justified by a general semantic argument, but is not part of the minimal proof boundary.
classification_vocabulary.reference_normalization: Deterministic semantic normalization required by the reference view.
classification_vocabulary.reference_projection: Rocq-alignment, exchange, or diagnostic view derived from the reference boundary; it is not the semantic source of obligations.
classification_vocabulary.obligation_preserving_optimization: Representation-only or proof-planning change that must preserve canonical obligations.
classification_vocabulary.backend: Target-specific projection, external proof execution, dumps, scheduling, profiling, or reporting.
classification_vocabulary.external_boundary: Boundary where an external tool may construct an input consumed by the reference kernel.

reference_kernel.description: Essential correction path from elaborated Kairos model plus supplied automata to canonical product states, product steps, and obligations. The reference product validates the automata normal form it consumes, while Spot construction remains outside this boundary. This is the part whose adequacy must be checked against the existing Rocq formalization.

forbidden_code_patterns.reason: Spot is an automata-construction adapter, not part of the reference kernel.
Why3 is a backend, not part of the reference kernel.
Z3 is an external prover, not part of the reference kernel.
Timing/profiling must stay outside the reference kernel.

exchange_views.description: Derived views used for diagnostics, cost reports, and possible Rocq synchronization after an adequacy decision. They must not define the essential theorem.

rocq_boundary.description: Architecture classification for checking adequacy with the existing Rocq formalization. This is not a generated Rocq theorem inventory.

stages.name: surface_elaboration
stages.rocq_role: Outside the current trusted kernel; a separate elaboration-correctness theorem may be added later.

stages.name: core_model
stages.rocq_role: Formal entry point for the elaborated Kairos program.

stages.name: historical_initialization_frontier
stages.rocq_role: Source well-formedness frontier for historical formulas. Rocq InitializationFrontier states the age contract; the OCaml validator enforces required_depth <= age using min_ticks_by_state as the current implementation witness, not as a certified algorithm.
allowed_effects: reject source formulas whose required historical depth exceeds the age available at their source point
compute source-point ages used by the validator
forbidden_effects: drop obligations after accepting a formula
weaken formulas to make them initialized
treat min_ticks_by_state as a Rocq-certified algorithm

stages.name: automata_generation
stages.rocq_role: Automata are inputs to the reference kernel; the formal story is relative to supplied automata and does not formalize Spot's LTL-to-automata translation. Product-boundary normal-form validation belongs to reference_product, not to this external generation stage.

stages.name: reference_product
stages.rocq_role: Program/product construction that must match the existing Rocq product-step semantics for adequacy, including validation of the supplied automata normal form consumed by product exploration.

stages.name: pre_requirements
stages.rocq_role: Generates source-state requirements for product-step obligations: state invariants, product-entry facts, assumption guards, program guards, and stability facts. Product-entry facts must satisfy the current-input-free architecture invariant expressed by Fo_current_input. These facts are part of the proof obligation shape; they must not be silently filtered by implementation convenience.
forbidden_effects: shift step-context guards into later ticks without a semantic argument

stages.name: product_reachability_obligations
stages.rocq_role: Adds preservation obligations for a generated reachability invariant. This is not pruning: the pass emits obligations such as guard => false. The essential Rocq boundary should see only the generic invariant principle, not this particular synthesis as a backend trick.
forbidden_effects: delete outgoing obligations from a source state
turn graph reachability into an unproved backend assumption

stages.name: post_ensures
stages.rocq_role: Generates destination obligations: safe successor disjunctions, destination invariants, guarded destination invariants, and product-characteristic preservation facts. These facts define the proof obligations for progression/correction.
forbidden_effects: weaken destination obligations for backend convenience

stages.name: temporal_lowering
stages.rocq_role: Materializes the temporal layout and rewrites pre/pre_k occurrences into explicit temporal bindings. This normalization must match the temporal model used by the existing Rocq formalization; it is not a backend optimization.
allowed_effects: rewrite summary formulas through temporal bindings
rewrite product-case guards through temporal bindings

stages.name: product_summary_projection
stages.rocq_role: Neutral OCaml projection for product-summary objects corresponding to ProofStepSummary and summary-case data. It is derived from Ir.node_ir and must stay independent from proof-export JSON and Why3.

stages.name: canonical_obligations
stages.rocq_role: Names the canonical Stage 1 clause family and Stage 2 step-contract family before proof_export, backend grouping, Why3 lowering, or diagnostics. This is the implementation-side object to compare with the Rocq proof principle.
allowed_effects: keep one bad-guarantee contract per unsafe case
forbidden_effects: split forbidden formulas for backend convenience

stages.name: obligation_family_projection
stages.rocq_role: Neutral semantic classification of generated obligation families. These are proof schemas, not diagnostic provenance tags.

stages.name: kernel_clause_projection
stages.rocq_role: Neutral OCaml projection for KernelClause, TimedFact, product anchors, and classified clause families before proof_export JSON, relational lowering, or Why3.

stages.name: step_contract_projection
stages.rocq_role: Derived grouped OCaml view of canonical Stage 2 contracts before Why3 helper naming, term sharing, or solver scheduling. It must be constructed from Canonical_obligations.stage2.

stages.name: formula_sharing
stages.rocq_role: No semantic role. This pass only reuses physically equal formula representatives for structurally equal top-level formulas.
allowed_effects: replace a formula by a structurally equal representative
preserve formula metadata shape except for physical identity

stages.name: proof_kernel_export
stages.rocq_role: Versioned exchange/projection data for diagnostics and possible Rocq synchronization after an explicit adequacy decision. It is not the semantic source of the theorem.

stages.name: runtime_orchestration
stages.rocq_role: Wiring, options, dumps, instrumentation, and proof-running are outside the Rocq kernel boundary.

stages.name: why3_backend
stages.rocq_role: Backend projection and external proof discharge; not the semantic source of obligations.
